title: Short Stuff: Cassowary
summary: Short Stuff episode on the cassowary, a large flightless bird native to Australia and New Guinea (Southeast Asia). The hosts cover its resemblance to dinosaurs, its dangerous 3-to-5-inch claws and kicks, its casque helmet and blue face and wattles, why it is flightless, its role as a keystone seed-disperser through fruit eating, its very low-pitched call, size and sex-role details (males raise chicks), conservation status, and wildlife overpasses. A brief mention is made of cassowaries kept as pets in Florida, where a man was killed by one.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the cassowary
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the cassowary as a flightless, dangerous bird from Australia, note its resemblance to dinosaurs and velociraptors, and describe its size and relation to emus and ostriches.

segments.title: Cassowary appearance and Florida pet deaths
segments.summary: The hosts describe the cassowary's casque, blue face, wattles and bristly feathers, and its Class two status in Florida, where a pet cassowary killed a 75-year-old man.

segments.title: Deadly claws, flightlessness and forest adaptations
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the danger comes from the three-to-five-inch claws and powerful kicks, why the wings are too small to fly, and how the casque and dense feathers help it move through thorny forest.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before returning to the cassowary topic.

segments.title: Threat level, wattle theories and keystone seed dispersal
segments.summary: The hosts say cassowaries are rarely aggressive toward people, discuss theories about the wattle as a mood or fitness signal, and explain their role as a keystone species that spreads seeds in their droppings.

segments.title: Size, sex roles, conservation and wildlife overpasses
segments.summary: The hosts give size figures, note that males raise the chicks, discuss declining populations and threats from habitat loss, cars and dogs, and mention conservation efforts and wildlife overpasses.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the short stuff episode and the show's production credit is read.
